explanation: Compare corresponding nodes recursively. Both must be null, or their values and both pairs of subtrees must agree.
timeComplexity: O(min(a, b)) node comparisons for trees with a and b nodes, stopping at the first mismatch.
spaceComplexity: O(h) recursion space up to the smaller traversed height.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Two empty positions match. If exactly one position is empty, the structures differ. Otherwise equal rooted trees require equal current values and equal corresponding left and right subtrees. These conditions are both necessary and sufficient, so recursive comparison is conclusive.
walkthrough: Compare [5,2] with [5,null,2]. Both roots have value 5, but the first tree has a left child 2 where the second has no child. The structural mismatch returns false even though both trees contain the same values.
edgeCases: Equal traversal values alone do not establish equal structure.
A mismatch can stop the comparison immediately.
